newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Soy shipping conditions at key Brazilian ports.
newsitem.headline: Soy shipping conditions at key Brazilian ports.

text.p: The key Brazilian ports of Paranagua and Santos reported the following conditions for shipping soybeans and soy products:
LOADING--Merak S loading 20,000 tonnes soymeal. Kanin loading 36,000 tonnes soymeal. Schubert loading 55,200 soymeal. Hunter loading 56,000 tonnes soybeans.
WAITING TO DOCK--10 vessels to load soybeans, 10 to load soymeal and two to load mixed cargoes (soybeans/corn and soybeans/meal).
ROAD--890 trucks unloaded soybeans on April 10, 253 trucks soymeal and 73 trucks vegetable oils, including soyoil.
LOADING--No figures available. The port loaded 1.1 million tonnes of soybeans in March, a new monthly record.

LOADING--Hilon of Sparta loading 61,000 tonnes, the largest single cargo of the year. At Cargill private terminal, Sea Challenger loading 36,000 tonnes soymeal. Three vessels waiting to dock to load soybeans.
ROAD--335 trucks carrying 8,909 tonnes soybeans arrived on April 10, as well as 16 trucks carrying 386 tonnes soymeal. RAIL--72 wagons arrived carrying 3,853 tonnes soybeans.

NOTE: Stevedores were working normally at the port, except at the private terminal of steel firm Companhia Siderurgica Paulista (Cosipa) where 26 stevedores continued to occupy two vessels, effectively paralyzing operations at the terminal.
